# About this example

Aelith is a fictional agglutinative language, built to walk through every module of Qonlang (all the data is invented and matches no real language):

- **Languages**: the family tree (Proto-Aelith → Aelith and its sister Merun under the “Ael 语系” node; click the family node for counts, phoneme correspondences, cognate ratios and a table of corresponding words), two historical stages inside Aelith (Classical CAe → Modern Ae, which the stage markers of “Proto → Aelith” are bound to), dialects, the alphabet
- **Phonology**: phonemes and features, classes generated from features, digraphs, two orthographies (the last line of the romanization → IPA rules, `ˈ = @ , <代词|小品词> 0 , 1`, is a stress rule, so the IPA comes out stressed: telikaso is read teliˈkaso by the special stress marked on its entry, and pronouns such as men and biz are unstressed), syllables and stress, phonotactics and word generation; the sister language Merun uses the custom stress rule `@ , -2 / _CC , -1` under “Syllables & prosody” — type hasta or hasu in the test to see where the stress falls; hara has special stress marked on its entry and stresses the first syllable
- **Script**: a runic inscription script, mapping rules, script forms typed by hand; “刻痕句读” was drawn on the glyph pad (open it and click “Edit drawing” to see the strokes)
- **Sound changes**: four rule sets (元音和谐 vowel harmony, Proto → Aelith, Proto → Merun, 书面语 → 口语 written → spoken), stages bound to languages, test word lists; “Proto → Aelith” has a rule with two branches for “environment matches / does not match” (`θ > t?s / #_`: t word-initially, s elsewhere) and a rule with two exclusions (`u > o / _# - k_ , g_`), and “Evolve lexicon” yields exactly the kaso, nöl and sör- in the lexicon; “书面语 → 口语” shows features (`[+浊] = b d g z v`, with the rule `[+浊] > [-浊] / _σ`), a stress rule (`ˈ = @ , <代词|小品词> 0 , 1`, so every column of the test bench carries ˈ; biz and sen are unstressed pronouns, telikaso stresses ka), the syllable boundary σ (unstressed e weakens: `e > ə / σ(C)(C)_ - ˈ(C)(C)_`, sen → sən) and two sounds merging into one (`{齿塞}=t d` against `{闪音}=r r`: t and d between vowels both become the flap r, kasoda → ˈkasora; r is written twice on the right so the classes match position by position)
- **Morphemes**: roots, prefixes, suffixes, infixes, circumfixes, clitics and particles; allomorph environments; etymology; “Affects stress”: the clitic =mU is unstressed and the prefix be- counts as an adjective
- **Lexicon**: in display mode, words inherited from the proto-language such as kaso and nöl show a line of historical forms above the examples (PAe kasu → CAe kaso → Ae kaso); several senses, several registers on one sense (dünar), dialects, tags, dimensions, compound parts of speech and a sense with its own part of speech (kara), stem slots, etymology chains (root, compound, derivation, sound change, loan, and a category of your own, “仿译” calque), a custom relation type (押韵 rhyme), images, hand-edited pronunciation, “Affects stress” (pronouns and particles pass on their part of speech, telikaso passes on its special stress); sörmek was created with “Add to lexicon” from the gerund of sör-, so its etymology and relations were filled in automatically; vesa deliberately has no definition, so it is marked red in the lexicon, and the issue counter at the right of the bottom bar jumps to it; kaso, nöl and sila are starred (the star at the left of the list; the star button at the top shows only them), and kaso and kel- carry a mark, a * in front of the word (the symbol is set in Settings → Basics); the inflected forms in the entry card are written with the dimensions’ gloss abbreviations (SG.NOM) — hover to see the full names
- **Relation graph**: in the relation graph of kaso, drag the empty space to move the canvas and right-click a node to expand or collapse it; “Compare” at the top right sets kaso (Aelith), hasu (Merun, where the meaning shifted to “tent”), kasolu and telikaso — all from the same root *kasu — side by side: the sound changes each went through, the k : h correspondence, and the differences in meaning and make-up
- **Inspector modules**: “文化注释” (cultural note) and “刻文异体” (inscription variant, shown in the inscription font), defined at the bottom of “Parts of speech & dimensions”; open kaso, nöl or sepe to see them
- **Paradigms**: all eight pipeline steps (prefix, suffix, infix, circumfix, sound change, pattern, reduplication, tweak), variants (the base set is renamed “书面” written), inheritance, disabled slots, tables filled by hand, “连读浊化” (sandhi voicing) that applies to all words (after ve, tovar → dovar; its “tweak” step defines a pair of classes on the spot, `{清塞}=p t k` and `{浊塞}=b d g`, matched by position), several paradigms for one part of speech (“verb” defaults to conjugation I; tur- and sal- pick conjugation II in their entries, and ol- uses the irregular one), letters that change by condition (the noun dative is written once as ¢{阴:g|k}A: the feminine sila and vene give silaga and venege, the others kasoka and the like), a paradigm nested in another (“gerund” adds -mAk and then goes through the cases of “noun”: sörmek, sörmekde), several paradigms on one entry (sör- both conjugates and has a gerund), slot inheritance (the plural accusative and locative of nouns continue from “复数.主格” kasolar and add the case suffix), allomorphs chosen by dimension value (the plural marker is -lAn before the dative: kasolanka), slot inheritance in simple mode (the third-person cells of verbs are left empty and continue from the two-dimension “polarity-tense” slots), pronunciation (the locative has its own pronunciation pipeline, where d between vowels is read ð: kasoda is read ˈkasoða), copying and pasting slots and whole variants, double-clicking a slot name to move a misplaced setup to another slot; the tabs are grouped by part of speech; switch the test bench to “Free” and type any form to see what it becomes
- **Corpus**: glossed and confirmed examples, another orthography, script forms typed by hand, free lines, sources and tags; dovar is recognised by working “连读浊化” backwards; ilenkasoda is two words written together plus a case suffix, and still splits without a separator; the name Mira is deliberately not in the lexicon, so hovering it says “Nothing found”; full stops and question marks in the text are shown as written and not counted as words; add a new example, click “Workbench” next to the translation and write 我知道你的朋友在房子里 (“I know your friend is in the house”): men, bil-, sen, tovar, kaso and other words float up below — drag them up in order and add the result to the corpus; click a word above to pick number and case in the attachment deck (kaso with the locative is kasoda), and drag the bubble “-(U)n 你的” onto tovar to make tovarun; 在 and 里 in the translation are flagged as having no matching word (Aelith uses the locative for “in”, so there is no need to create one); type a new word under “Not in the lexicon? Type it”, choose noun, and it declines like a noun
- **Phrasebook**: categories, variants, pronunciation, placeholders in square brackets
- **Docs**: project-level and language-level pages; write `[[kaso]]` to link to a word in the lexicon; the page “Aelith grammar sketch” also uses `[[morpheme:-lAr]]`, `[[soundchange:Proto → Aelith#现代语]]` and `[[paradigm:noun#单数.位格]]` — with a prefix a link can point to a morpheme, a language, a script, one stage of a sound change or one cell of a paradigm (prefixes work in English and in Chinese, e.g. `[[语素:-lAr]]`; “Insert link” on the toolbar lets you pick)
- **Settings**: export templates, the abbreviation list

For an isolating language with tones, a syllabary and vertical writing, open the other example, **Tsahun**.

Aelith 语法概要.title: Aelith grammar sketch
Aelith 语法概要.markdown:
# Aelith grammar sketch

## Phonology
- Seven vowels in a back and a front set: a o u / e ö ü, with i neutral.
- A and U in suffixes take the backness of the last vowel of the word (see [[soundchange:元音和谐|vowel harmony]]).
- The chain from the proto-language: [[soundchange:Proto → Aelith#现代语|Proto → Aelith, modern stage]]; for the inscription spelling see [[script:Aelith 刻文|the Aelith inscription script]], and for the sister language see [[language:Merun]].

## Nouns
Root-number-case: plural [[morpheme:-lAr]], accusative [[morpheme:-(U)m]], locative [[morpheme:-dA]], dative [[morpheme:-kA]]; feminine nouns ([[sila]], [[vene]]) take -gA in the dative, written once in the paradigm as ¢{阴:g|k}A. The full declension is in [[paradigm:noun]]; the singular locative cell is [[paradigm:noun#单数.位格|noun · singular locative]].

| | Singular | Plural |
|---|---|---|
| Nominative | [[kaso]] | kasolar |
| Locative | kasoda | kasolarda |

## Verbs
Root-negation-tense-person: `sör-me-dü-m` “I did not see”. The third person is unmarked; the negative present third person uses a periphrasis (disabled in the paradigm).

Two conjugations: conjugation I forms the past with -dU (sördüm), conjugation II with -tI (tur- → turtim, sal- → saltim).

## Questions
The sentence-final clitic =mU: `sen kelsen mü`.

## Sandhi
After the particle ve, word-initial p t k become voiced: `ilen ve dovar` ([[tovar]] “friend”). The paradigm “连读浊化” (sandhi voicing) applies to all words, and the corpus works it backwards to the base form when splitting words.

祖语拟构说明.markdown:
# Notes on the proto-language

The root list is on the Morphemes page; “Sound changes → Proto → Aelith” gives the rules down to the modern language, and “Evolve lexicon” derives the whole list: word-final u lowers to o (*kasu → kaso, but not after k or g), o in a word-final closed syllable fronts to ö (*nol → nöl, *sor → sör-), and θ becomes t word-initially and s elsewhere (*θura → tura).

# About this example

Tsahun is a fictional isolating tone language that complements the other example, **Aelith**, and shows these features in particular:

- **Tone**: the prosody type is set to “tone”, and each of the five tones has a tone mark and a number; the first rule of the romanization → IPA conversion is tone sandhi, `35 > ˧?˧˥ / _C , _V` (two branches for “environment matches / does not match”), so the reduplicated lun35lun35 is read lun˧lun˧˥
- **Two orthographies**: romanization (tones as numbers) and a Cyrillic spelling, and examples can show both side by side; the phoneme table gives each phoneme’s romanized spelling, so the “Syllables & prosody” test counts ts and ng as one sound each when you type tsang55, and the intensive reduplication of the adjective tsing55 gives tsitsing55 (counting letters would give tstsing55)
- **Script**: a syllabary that **combines** signs (consonant + vowel join into one cell automatically, a final consonant uses a vowel killer) and is **written vertically**
- **Paradigms**: isolating languages have paradigms too — reduplication forms plurals and intensives; plural pronouns add `@tui55` after a space (when the morpheme list has no such morpheme, the entry of the same name is used), giving `ngo21 tui55` with a space
- **Corpus**: reduplicated forms are glossed automatically too (`lun35lun35`), and `ngo21 tui55` with its space is recognised as one word; the homograph in `hok33 lo21` is deliberately left unconfirmed, so hovering it shows the candidates side by side; click a verb in the workbench and the attachment deck lists the particles the corpus has used with verbs: the perfective ta33 goes after it and the negative mo35 before it (on whichever side they usually stand in the corpus)
- **Lexicon**: minimal pairs that differ only in tone, the homograph hok33 (red / learn), compounds, a whole set of borrowed numerals, several registers on one sense (hu35)
- **Inspector modules**: “异体字” (variant character) is shown above the definition in the syllabary font (wa55), and “语用说明” (usage note) goes at the bottom (lo21, ta33)
- **Bracket settings of a script**: the syllabary is set to “leave out the brackets and their contents”, so in the phrase `ni33 hem55 (lo21)` the script line has no bracketed part
- **A logographic script written by sign number**: each sign of “Tsahun 刻符” is transcribed as a sign number (k01, k02 …), not a reading; the inspector module “字号” (sign number) of an entry says which signs write the word (wa55 is `k04 k03`), and the script page’s “Transcribe from” is set to that module. The script column of the lexicon and the script lines of the corpus and phrasebook look each word up in the lexicon: `ngo21 kwe51 ta33 sip51` is written ⼰ ⼝ ta33 ⿂, and function words without a sign number are left as they are

Tsahun 语法概要.title: Tsahun grammar sketch
Tsahun 语法概要.markdown:
# Tsahun grammar sketch

## Tones
Five tones: 55 high level, 35 rising, 21 low falling, 51 falling, 33 mid level. The same syllable with a different tone is a different word: [[tsa55]] “water” / [[tsa21]] “fire”.

Tone sandhi: tone 35 is read 33 when another syllable follows, so the reduplicated `lun35lun35` is read lun˧lun˧˥.

## Word order
SVO; possession is linked with ka55: `ta51 ka55 wa55` “his house”.

## Aspect and negation
The perfective ta33 follows the verb; the negative mo35 precedes it.

## Plural
Nouns reduplicate as a whole: `lun35lun35` “people”. Pronouns are followed by [[tui55]]: `ngo21 tui55` “we”.
